prompts.situation: A friend has been offered a promotion that pays more but means moving to another city, away from their family and their long-time hockey team.
prompts.instruction: Give your friend advice about whether to accept the promotion. Explain your reasons.
bullets: What matters most in this decision
What they might regret either way
What you would do and why

prompts.situation: Think about a time when you had to learn something quickly, with very little help.
prompts.instruction: Describe that experience. Say what you had to learn, how you managed it, and how it turned out.
bullets: When and where it happened
What made it difficult
What you would do differently now

prompts.situation: You are describing a photograph to someone who cannot see it. The photograph shows a busy neighbourhood library on a rainy Saturday afternoon.
prompts.instruction: Describe what is happening in the scene so the listener can picture it clearly.
bullets: Who is there and what they are doing
Where things are in relation to each other
The overall mood of the scene

prompts.situation: In the same library scene, a staff member is standing on a chair reaching for a box on the top shelf, and a child is running along the aisle underneath.
prompts.instruction: Predict what will happen next in the scene, and explain what leads you to think so.
bullets: What you expect to happen first
How the people nearby will react
How it is likely to end

prompts.situation: You want to buy a used car for your family. There is a small hatchback with low mileage and excellent fuel economy, and an older van with more space but higher running costs. Your partner will make the final decision.
prompts.instruction: Choose one of the two options and persuade your partner that it is the better choice.
bullets: Why your choice suits your family
What the other option costs you
What you are willing to compromise on

prompts.situation: Your neighbour lent you a ladder two months ago. It was damaged in a storm while it was at your house. Your neighbour is friendly but particular about their tools, and they have just asked for it back.
prompts.instruction: Choose ONE of the following, and speak directly to that person: explain the situation to your neighbour, OR ask a family member to help you deal with it.
bullets: Say clearly who you are speaking to
Explain what happened
Say what you propose to do about it

prompts.situation: Your city is considering closing one downtown street permanently to cars, turning it into a space for walking, patios, and events. Local shop owners are divided.
prompts.instruction: State your opinion on the proposal and support it with reasons.
bullets: Your position, stated clearly
Two reasons that support it
One objection and your response to it

prompts.situation: You have found an unfamiliar object at a garage sale: a wooden box about the size of a shoebox, with a hinged lid, a small crank on one side, and three brass dials on the front. Nobody at the sale knows what it is.
prompts.instruction: Describe the object to a friend on the phone, precisely enough that they can picture it, and say what you think it might be for.
bullets: Size, shape, and material
The parts you can see and how they might work
What you think it does and why
